blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, what is the main reason to hand a `Runnable` to a `Thread` rather than subclass `Thread`?

options.text: It lets one Thread object be started again, once its first run has ended
options.says: The page says calling start() on a thread that has already finished throws IllegalThreadStateException.

options.text: It keeps the task apart from how it runs, and leaves the inheritance slot free
options.says: The page says Runnable separates task logic from thread management and lets the class still extend another class.

options.text: It makes start() unnecessary, since the task's run() creates the thread itself
options.says: The page says calling run() executes on the current thread and creates no new thread; start() is what creates it.

questions.stem: Per this page, what happens to a daemon thread that is still running when the JVM exits?

options.text: It is allowed to finish its current task, and then the JVM shuts down
options.says: The page says the JVM exits once all non-daemon threads finish, even if daemon threads are still running.

options.text: It is interrupted and its finally blocks run, and then the JVM shuts down
options.says: The page says daemon threads are not interrupted and their finally blocks do not run.

options.text: It is abandoned and its finally blocks are skipped, and then the JVM shuts down
options.says: The page says daemon threads are abandoned abruptly: they are not interrupted, and their finally blocks do not run.

concepts: At JVM exit daemon threads are abandoned abruptly: they are not interrupted and their finally blocks do not run.
Implementing Runnable is preferred to extending Thread, because it leaves the inheritance slot free and separates the task from how it runs.
